description: This test validates that the MurmurHash3 hash algorithm produces consistent 128-bit hash values when processing the same string data through different input methods, specifically comparing byte array input versus direct string input to ensure hash computation equivalence. The test iterates one thousand times, each time generating a random Unicode string and computing its hash through both pathways to assert that the results are identical. Initialize a seed value of 104729 for the hash function, set minimum string size to 1 and maximum size to 11 characters, and define the Unicode code point range as 112956 to cover Unicode Standard Version 7.0 characters. Create a character array with capacity for the maximum possible string length accounting for surrogate pairs. For each iteration, use ThreadLocalRandom to generate a random string size between the minimum and maximum bounds, then populate the character array by generating random Unicode code points and converting them to characters using the Character toChars method, tracking the position as characters are added to handle variable-width Unicode encoding. Create a string from the populated character array using String copyValueOf with the actual character count. Convert the generated string to a UTF-8 byte array using StringUtils getBytesUtf8 method. Compute the 128-bit hash of the byte array using MurmurHash3 hash128 method with the byte array, starting offset of 0, the full byte array length, and the predefined seed. Compute the 128-bit hash of the original string directly using the overloaded MurmurHash3 hash128 method that accepts a string parameter. Assert that both hash results are equal using assertArrayEquals to validate that the hash128 method produces identical output regardless of whether the input is provided as a byte array or string. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.
